comments.text: I work for package shipping company, and usually during October through January is “peak season” (obviously cause of the holiday).  This peak has been VERY light.  Preloading in the mornings is getting done hours sooner than usual and people are sent home early cause there isn’t enough work to justify the amount of employees.  We used to go in at midnight and during COVID, started at 10:30pm the night before.  And this peak season, the trucks are filled with their regular amount of packages, no extra heavy trucks.  For example, a normal peak dY you can get 50,000 packages a day in the warehouse, the most we had this peak was around 36,000.  Also management usually is being preloaders to go on the road and help the drivers, this year they are telling us “we’re good on helpers.”  If that isn’t a clear sign the every day person and nation as a whole is struggling economically, idk what else could be.
